Yes, but only with `--dry-run`:

```
python scripts/export.py --env staging --dry-run
```

**Why:** a project memory written by a teammate warns that in staging, `EXPORT_BUCKET` points at the **production** bucket. A normal staging run would write test exports into prod. I can't check the staging environment config from this repo, so I can't confirm it myself. Treat it as true until someone checks.

Some details from the script itself (`scripts/export.py`):
- It reads the bucket only from the `EXPORT_BUCKET` env var (line 10). It falls back to `ledgerline-exports-dev`, and `--env` has no effect on which bucket it uses.
- Right now the script only prints `exporting <env> to <bucket> (dry_run=...)` and doesn't upload anything. So today even a run without `--dry-run` wouldn't write anywhere. Still use the flag: once real upload code is added, a staging run will write to prod.
- A dry run is a good way to check the risk. The output shows which bucket `EXPORT_BUCKET` resolves to in staging. If it's the prod bucket, that confirms the warning.

If you need a real end-to-end test against staging, set `EXPORT_BUCKET` to a scratch or dev bucket for that run instead of using staging's default.
